content.text: King Robert meets Albany, March, Douglas, and Rothsay at the Dominican monastery palace in Perth. Rothsay’s misconduct toward the minstrel Louise provokes Douglas; Henry Smith escorts Louise through secret passages, the church, monastery gardens, and Perth to his house, where Nurse Shoolbred shelters her. Meanwhile, Ramorny and Dwining plot revenge, and Bonthron murders Oliver Proudfute, mistaking him for Smith. Perth’s citizens gather in the streets and council house, demand justice, and appoint Smith as the widow’s champion. At St. John’s Church, Bonthron refuses bier-right and fights Smith in the Skinners’ Yards, where he is defeated and confesses. He falsely implicates Rothsay, deepening political danger as Albany urges the people to believe the accusation.
